outcome: Balance skill, latency, wait time, party needs and fairness to create healthier multiplayer sessions
overview: Simple multiplayer queues trade long waits against poor latency or unfair matches, and players answer with abandonment, toxicity and competitive distrust. This solution treats matchmaking as constrained optimisation: skill, latency, wait time, party composition and fairness constraints are balanced to create healthier sessions, with published matchmaking principles, hard constraints and full audit. A shadow deployment scores real queues without touching live matches; only after replay and back-testing does a controlled rollout begin, with rollback ready. An 8–12-week proof of value targets shorter queues, better latency and improved match-quality measures. Reference builds are specified for AWS and Azure, with Gulf server regions for regional latency.

benefits.text: Reduce queue time or session latency at equal or better match balance
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Validated in shadow mode against the customer’s own queues before any live claim — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Improve agreed match-quality and fairness measures, cutting early quits and disconnect rates
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on skill-model quality and regional player density at each hour of day

benefits.text: Give competitive-integrity teams an auditable, published matchmaking policy instead of a black box
benefits.source: Reference design capability, Redington Gaming catalogue
benefits.limits: Auditability covers the optimisation constraints; it does not by itself detect smurfing or boosting

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA, Bahrain); match and player data remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No recorded match outcomes or skill signal to optimise against
notFor.why: Constrained optimisation needs historical outcomes to validate against; without them no configuration can be back-tested honestly

notFor.situation: Single-region titles with thin concurrent population
notFor.why: With few concurrent players the queue has no meaningful trade-off space; optimisation cannot conjure opponents

notFor.situation: No shadow-test or rollback capability in the matchmaking path
notFor.why: Changing live matchmaking without shadow validation risks the competitive trust the solution exists to protect

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns matchmaking principles and competitive-integrity approval · Duration: 8–12-week shadow PoV; further 16–26 weeks to full production
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, matchmaking engineer, network specialist; customer gameplay director, SRE lead, competitive-integrity reviewer, analytics lead · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and match-quality baseline agreement
2) Queue and telemetry integration
3) Constraint modelling and replay back-testing
4) Shadow deployment against live queues
5) Controlled regional rollout with rollback ready
6) Stabilisation and handover
